rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A lichen is a dual organism: a fungus (usually an ascomycete) that builds the thallus, absorbs water and minerals and shields its partner, and an alga or cyanobacterium (*Trebouxia*, *Nostoc*) that photosynthesises — and fixes nitrogen in cyanolichens. Thalli are crustose, foliose or fruticose; reproduction runs from soredia and isidia to fungal ascospores that must re-capture an alga.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Crustose lichens lie flat on rock, foliose ones are leafy, and fruticose ones hang or stand, as Usnea does on temperate branches in Nepal.
Lichens colonise bare rock, indicate polluted air because many of them disappear when the air is foul, and some supply dye or fodder. The fungus usually takes the name. The alga makes the sugar.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Symbiosis vs parasitism in lichens:** the association is mutualistic (both benefit); the fungus may slightly control the alga, but the classic teaching is mutualism.  ·  **Soredia vs isidia:** soredia are powdery, microscopic, loose; isidia are compact outgrowths of the thallus surface — both carry both partners.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Match the organism to the character.  ·  A product does not move an organism into another kingdom.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Usnea longissima*** — old man's beard; fruticose; medicinal usnic acid.  ·  ***Cladonia rangiferina*** — reindeer moss; arctic fodder.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What are soredia? **Answer.** Powder-like **vegetative propagules** of lichens: one or a few **algal cells wrapped in fungal hyphae**, escaping from a soralium on the thallus surface. Wind carries them off, and each soredium can grow into a new lichen — they disperse the **intact symbiosis**, both partners together.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Mutualism enables extremes:** fungal shelter + algal food = an organism that survives desiccation, cold and bare rock — neither partner could.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Lichen = mycobiont (fungus, usually ascomycete) + phycobiont (*Trebouxia* alga or *Nostoc* cyanobacterium).  ·  Growth forms: crustose (*Lecanora*), foliose (*Parmelia*), fruticose (*Usnea*, *Cladonia*).  ·  Structure (foliose): upper cortex — algal layer — medulla — lower cortex with rhizines.  ·  Reproduction: fragmentation, soredia, isidia (vegetative); conidia; ascospores via apothecia (sexual, fungus only).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Litmus indicator dye comes from lichens — a laboratory staple since the 17th century.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Roccella montagnei*** — source of litmus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Importance: reindeer food, litmus dye (*Roccella*), usnic-acid medicine, perfumes, **air-pollution bioindicators** (SO₂ sensitive), pioneer rock weatherers, nitrogen fixation by cyanolichens.  ·  **Lichen vs moss:** lichens are dual fungi-algae; mosses are true bryophyte plants.  ·  Always answer lichen questions with BOTH partners named and BOTH roles stated — single-partner answers lose half marks.
